brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases: full bases piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 and piece:0,1,0 plus a half-e base piece:-1,0,0 forming a compact cluster. Lock joints and end caps applied; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at notch:0#0,-1 (k=4), filling the empty spot beside the bases at (0,0) and (1,0)-side. Drawer frame is part of the build; no props placed in it.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 sits at the junction of bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0).
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that spike (a solid spike refused platforms, so a mount-variant spike was used).

finish.summary: Built a compact four-base desk cluster with a notch drawer frame and a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. Joints locked, open faces capped, configurator check clean. No props added. Drawer is a frame with no bin or drawer front placed in it.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
